headline: Patent Issued for System and method for fairness aware optimization with features quantization (USPTO 12639338)
story_html:
2026 JUN 11-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Math Daily News-- JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. has been issued patent number 12639338, according to news reporting originating out of Alexandria, Virginia, by NewsRx editors. The patent' s inventors are Bollum, Dan, Brugere, Ivan, Hosking, Michael, Kapadia, Deven R, Lecue, Freddy, Liang, Lei Carol, Stettler, John, Tan, Yue, Zhao,... 2026 JUN 11 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Math Daily News -- JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. (New York, New York, United States) has been issued patent number 12639338, according to news reporting originating out of Alexandria, Virginia, by NewsRx editors.

The patent's inventors are Bollum, Dan (Westerville, DE, US), Brugere, Ivan (Des Plaines, IL, US), Hosking, Michael (Columbus, OH, US), Kapadia, Deven R (Yorba Linda, CA, US), Lecue, Freddy (Mamaroneck, NY, US), Liang, Lei Carol (Hamburg, NJ, US), Stettler, John (Columbus, OH, US), Tan, Yue (Lewis Center, DE, US), Zhao, Huiyan (Plano, TX, US), Zweier, Joseph (Columbus, OH, US).

This patent was filed on March 5, 2025 and was published online on May 26, 2026.

From the background information supplied by the inventors, news correspondents obtained the following quote: "The developments described in this section are known to the inventors. However, unless otherwise indicated, it should not be assumed that any of the developments described in this section qualify as prior art merely by virtue of their inclusion in this section, or that these developments are known to a person of ordinary skill in the art.

"Presently, various algorithms and machine learning models may be applied to numerous variables in decision making for obtaining optimal results in various applications. For example, a conventional algorithm or machine learning model may be focused on finding a balance between value and volume to maximize output for an organization as illustrated in FIG. 9. However, such conventional approach to optimization by the algorithms and machine learning models may lead to disparate results for certain protected attributes (e.g., sex, race, age) without intention and may potentially violate one or more government regulations and/or organizational operating policies.

"Although an embedded bias in an algorithm or machine learning model may result in disparate outcome for certain protected attributes, even algorithms or machine learning model without such embedded bias may still provide disparate outcomes, which may run afoul of the one or more government regulations and/or organization policies.

"As illustrated in FIG. 10, a conventional optimization model may apply plus or minus basis points (bps) adjustments to base pricing based on various features of a loan application to maximize profit and losses (P&L) Features of the loan application may include a particular credit score associated with the application, which may have corresponding ranges of bps adjustments possible for maximizing profit. Although the bps adjustments may be applied to maximize P&L in the example of FIG. 10, such optimization may unwittingly result in providing disparate results for certain protected groups of people having certain race, ethnicity, gender or the like, and run afoul of one or more government regulations and/or organizational operating policies.

"Accordingly, for real-world applications, there is a need for computer or machine learning models that are capable of performing optimizations while avoiding disparate outcomes for one or more protected attributes, which are conventionally unavailable."

Supplementing the background information on this patent, NewsRx reporters also obtained the inventors' summary information for this patent: "The present disclosure, through one or more of its various aspects, embodiments, and/or specific features or sub-components, provides, among other features, a method for performing a fairness aware optimization on a plurality of attributes is provided. The method includes acquiring, by a processor and from a plurality of databases, an input dataset including a plurality of applications with corresponding set of input features, wherein each of the plurality of applications has a plurality of input features; quantizing, by the processor, each of the plurality of input features for the plurality of applications; performing binning, by the processor, of each of the plurality of input features quantized so that each of the plurality of input features for each of the plurality of applications is assigned to a bin among a plurality of bins to provide a matrix of bin membership for each of the plurality of applications; querying, by the processor, a machine learning (ML) model for generating a vector for each of the plurality of applications based on a corresponding matrix of bin membership; evaluating, via the ML model and for an application of the plurality of applications, the generated vector against a corresponding target value and presence of disparity in outcome for one or more of the plurality of input features, wherein the evaluating includes: generating one or more function parameters for the corresponding matrix of bin membership; generating a coefficient vector based on the one or more function parameters; generating the corresponding target value based on the matrix of bin membership and the generated coefficient vector; calculating a predicted output for the input dataset in view of the corresponding target value; and calculating for the presence of disparity in outcome for at least one of the plurality of input features; performing iterations of the evaluating, on the ML model and for remaining applications of the plurality of applications until completion; identifying, by the ML model, a target coefficient vector among a plurality of coefficient vectors generated for the plurality of applications that provides an optimized output while negating the presence of disparity in outcome; updating the ML model with the target coefficient vector; and applying the updated ML model on a subsequent application, wherein the updated ML model provides an output without disparate outcome for any input feature of the subsequent application.

"In some embodiments, each of the plurality of bins are defined by a pair of boundary values.

"In some embodiments, the plurality of bins are of equal size.

"In some embodiments, the plurality of bins include bins of uneven sizes.

"In some embodiments, the ML model is a Bayesian optimization model."

The claims supplied by the inventors are:

"1. A method for performing a fairness aware optimization on a plurality of attributes, the method comprising: acquiring, by a processor and from a plurality of databases, an input dataset including a plurality of applications with corresponding set of input features, wherein each of the plurality of applications has a plurality of input features; quantizing, by the processor, each of the plurality of input features for the plurality of applications; performing binning, by the processor, of each of the plurality of input features quantized so that each of the plurality of input features for each of the plurality of applications is assigned to a bin among a plurality of bins to provide a matrix of bin membership for each of the plurality of applications; querying, by the processor, a machine learning (ML) model for generating a vector for each of the plurality of applications based on a corresponding matrix of bin membership, wherein each of the plurality of bins is associated with a corresponding vector, such that each of the plurality of applications is characterized by a plurality of vectors based on the matrix of bin membership; evaluating, via the ML model and for an application of the plurality of applications, the generated vector against a corresponding target value and presence of disparity in outcome for one or more of the plurality of input features, wherein the evaluating includes: generating one or more function parameters for the corresponding matrix of bin membership; generating a coefficient vector based on the one or more function parameters; generating the corresponding target value based on the matrix of bin membership and the generated coefficient vector; calculating a predicted output for the input dataset in view of the corresponding target value; and calculating for the presence of disparity in outcome for at least one of the plurality of input features; performing one or more training iterations of the evaluating, on the ML model and for remaining applications of the plurality of applications until an offset value for each bin that adjusts a regression target for input features grouped into a particular bin is determined; identifying, by the ML model and based on performance of the one or more training iterations on the ML model, a target coefficient vector among a plurality of coefficient vectors generated for the plurality of applications that provides an optimized output while negating the presence of disparity in outcome; storing one or more function parameters including the identified target coefficient vector, and updating the ML model with the target coefficient vector, wherein the stored one or more function parameters approximate an objective function of the ML model to limit search space for more efficient exploration with respect to unobserved points; and applying the updated ML model on a subsequent application, wherein the updated ML model applies the offset at a bin level to provide an output without disparate outcome for any input feature of the subsequent application.

"2. The method according to claim 1, wherein each of the plurality of bins are defined by a pair of boundary values.

"3. The method according to claim 1, wherein the plurality of bins are of equal size.

"4. The method according to claim 1, wherein the plurality of bins include bins of uneven sizes.

"5. The method according to claim 1, wherein the ML model is a Bayesian optimization model.

"6. The method according to claim 1, wherein each of the plurality of applications has its input features assigned to less than all of the plurality of bins.

"7. The method according to claim 1, wherein the optimized output refers to a highest output value that negates the presence of disparity in outcome for a protected feature among the plurality of input features.

"8. The method according to claim 7, wherein the protected feature is a feature regulated by a government entity.

"9. The method according to claim 7, wherein the protected feature is a race of an applicant of at least one of the plurality of applications.

"10. The method according to claim 7, wherein the protected feature is a gender of an applicant of at least one of the plurality of applications.

"11. A system for performing a fairness aware optimization on a plurality of attributes, the system comprising: a processor; and a memory operatively connected to the processor via a communication interface, the memory storing computer readable instructions, when executed, causes the processor to perform: acquiring, from a plurality of databases, an input dataset including a plurality of applications with corresponding set of input features, wherein each of the plurality of applications has a plurality of input features; quantizing each of the plurality of input features for the plurality of applications; performing binning of each of the plurality of input features quantized so that each of the plurality of input features for each of the plurality of applications is assigned to a bin among a plurality of bins to provide a matrix of bin membership for each of the plurality of applications; querying a machine learning (ML) model for generating a vector for each of the plurality of applications based on a corresponding matrix of bin membership, wherein each of the plurality of bins is associated with a corresponding vector, such that each of the plurality of applications is characterized by a plurality of vectors based on the matrix of bin membership; evaluating, via the ML model and for an application of the plurality of applications, the generated vector against a corresponding target value and presence of disparity in outcome for one or more of the plurality of input features, wherein the evaluating includes: generating one or more function parameters for the corresponding matrix of bin membership; generating a coefficient vector based on the one or more function parameters; generating the corresponding target value based on the matrix of bin membership and the generated coefficient vector; calculating a predicted output for the input dataset in view of the corresponding target value; and calculating for the presence of disparity in outcome for at least one of the plurality of input features; performing one or more training iterations of the evaluating, on the ML model and for remaining applications of the plurality of applications until an offset value for each bin that adjusts a regression target for input features grouped into a particular bin is determined; identifying, by the ML model and based on performance of the one or more training iterations on the ML model, a target coefficient vector among a plurality of coefficient vectors generated for the plurality of applications that provides an optimized output while negating the presence of disparity in outcome; storing one or more function parameters including the identified target coefficient vector, and updating the ML model with the target coefficient vector, wherein the stored one or more function parameters approximate an objective function of the ML model to limit search space for more efficient exploration with respect to unobserved points; and applying the updated ML model on a subsequent application, wherein the updated ML model applies the offset at a bin level to provide an output without disparate outcome for any input feature of the subsequent application.

"12. The system according to claim 11, wherein each of the plurality of bins are defined by a pair of boundary values.

"13. The system according to claim 11, wherein the plurality of bins are of equal size.

"14. The system according to claim 11, wherein the plurality of bins include bins of uneven sizes.

"15. The system according to claim 11, wherein the ML model is a Bayesian optimization model.

"16. The system according to claim 11, wherein the optimized output refers to a highest output value that negates the presence of disparity in outcome for a protected feature among the plurality of input features.

"17. The system according to claim 16, wherein the protected feature is a feature regulated by a government entity.

"18. The system according to claim 16, wherein the protected feature is a race of an applicant of at least one of the plurality of applications.

"19. The system according to claim 16, wherein the protected feature is a gender of an applicant of at least one of the plurality of applications."

headline: U.S. banks are allowing employees to work from home to avoid traffic chaos during the World Cup
story_html:
Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase are temporarily relaxing their in-office work requirements for employees during the World Cup, as workers brace for transportation disruptions and increased traffic congestion in host cities during the world's largest sporting event.

According to people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street banks have informed employees that they may request permission to work from home on match days, after warning of potential travel difficulties in host cities, including New York.

Hundreds of thousands of soccer fans are expected in New York and New Jersey in the coming weeks, as the region will host eight World Cup matches, including a final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan have been two of the most vocal opponents of remote work on Wall Street in recent years.

David Solomon, CEO of Goldman Sachs, had previously called working from home an "aberration," while JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon harshly criticized remote work policies in a profanity-laced speech during an internal meeting last year.

Citigroup, which has maintained a flexible work policy since the start of the pandemic, has also encouraged employees in hybrid roles to work remotely in World Cup host cities during the tournament, people familiar with the matter said.

According to a memo reviewed by the Financial Times, JPMorgan's temporary policy applies to all employees in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico.

The temporary concessions underscore the logistical challenges posed by the month-long soccer tournament, which is expected to place significant strain on transportation networks in the host countries.

The measures also suggest that, although banks are ordering employees to return to the office full-time, remote work remains a useful contingency tool for indirect management, even for the most office-focused firms on Wall Street.

Goldman Sachs was one of the first major banks to end remote work during the pandemic in 2021, while JPMorgan planned last year for most employees to return to the office five days a week.

Residents in host cities were advised to prepare for heavier traffic and longer commute times, as millions of fans traveled between games, fan zones, and city centers.

In New York, the train connecting Penn Station to Secaucus Junction in New Jersey—near MetLife Stadium, which will be renamed New York New Jersey Stadium during the tournament—will be restricted to World Cup ticket holders for four hours before the start of matches.

Major sporting events often prompt warnings that transportation networks will struggle to handle the influx of visitors.

Before the 2012 London Olympics, there were fears of "Olympic chaos" due to concerns that the capital's transportation infrastructure would not withstand the pressure. Although the Summer Games caused some disruptions, those fears proved unfounded.

Economists at Goldman Sachs predicted that Spain is the favorite to win the World Cup, giving the country a 26% chance of lifting the trophy on July 19, ahead of France and Argentina.

Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Citi declined to comment.

June 10 2026: JPMorgan Secures Temporary Restraining Order Against Morgan Stanley Advisors

JPMorgan Chase & Co. has successfully obtained a temporary restraining order (TRO) from a New York state court, effectively barring two former brokers from soliciting clients they had engaged with during their tenure at the firm. This ruling came on 11th June 2026, as JPMorgan's legal team argued that the brokers, Christopher J. Lee and Joseph S. Minaudo, had managed $1.85 billion in assets across 1,350 client households before their recent transition to Morgan Stanley in late May.

The court's order prevents Lee and Minaudo from reaching out to clients representing a total of $84 million in assets who have already begun to follow them to Morgan Stanley. According to JPMorgan's claims, the duo had been aggressively soliciting their former clients, offering incentives such as exclusive access to initial public offerings and enhanced financial benefits, which they described as a 'full court press'. This aggressive client acquisition effort has raised concerns within JPMorgan regarding the potential loss of valuable client relationships.

The ruling was handed down by New York County Supreme Court Judge Lyle E. Frank, who acknowledged JPMorgan's concerns. Under the regulations set by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), brokerages must secure a TRO to expedite arbitration for damages and seek a permanent injunction within 15 days. Legal experts note that such cases often lead to settlements or mediation before the hearings occur, which could be a possibility in this situation.

Jonathan Thau, the attorney representing Lee and Minaudo, expressed confidence in their case, asserting that the brokers had adhered to their employment contracts and industry best practices. He emphasized that the allegations made by JPMorgan were unfounded, pointing out that the bank had included sensitive information in its court documents, which was later redacted. This incident reflects the contentious nature of such legal disputes in the finance sector, particularly when high-profile teams transition between firms.

The departure of Lee and Minaudo, previously celebrated by JPMorgan as part of its successful advisory teams, raises questions about the firm's retention strategies. While JPMorgan allows traditional brokers at J.P. Morgan Advisors to solicit clients when moving to another firm within the Protocol, it restricts its private client advisors from similar practices. This case underscores the ongoing challenges facing financial institutions in maintaining client loyalty amidst competitive recruiting practices from rival firms like Morgan Stanley.

June 10 2026: JPMorgan's Strategic Investment in Charm Industrial Signals Carbon Market Maturity

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is making strides in the evolving carbon removal market through a new agreement with Charm Industrial. This deal, which was finalized on the 10th of June, 2026, marks a pivotal moment as carbon removal transitions from pilot projects to scalable solutions. Under the terms of the agreement, JPMorgan will purchase 61,500 metric tons of carbon removal credits from Charm Industrial, while also providing financial support aimed at expanding the company's operational capacity.

The JPMorgan-Charm Industrial partnership underscores a significant trend among large financial institutions that increasingly view carbon removal as both a climate solution and a burgeoning market opportunity. As companies worldwide gear up to meet net-zero targets, the demand for high-quality carbon removal credits continues to surge. Taylor Wright, Head of Operational Sustainability at JPMorgan Chase, emphasized the importance of this purchase, stating it reflects the bank's maturing portfolio and commitment to impactful carbon removal solutions.

Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) differs from traditional carbon offsets, focusing on the permanent extraction of CO2 from the atmosphere. Experts agree that emissions reductions alone will not suffice to meet global climate objectives. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change warns that achieving a global temperature increase limited to 1.5degC will necessitate large-scale carbon removal efforts. Current global demand for engineered carbon removals is still below 10 million metric tons annually, while overall removals, primarily from forestry, are at 2.2 billion tons. Projections indicate that demand could reach billions of tons annually by mid-century, particularly from hard-to-decarbonize sectors such as aviation and steel.

The JPMorgan-Charm agreement aligns with the bank's broader climate strategy, which includes a commitment to net-zero emissions by 2050 and a pledge to finance over $2.5 trillion in sustainable development initiatives by 2030. The structure of the deal is noteworthy; rather than solely purchasing carbon credits, JPMorgan is also facilitating future production capacity. This model provides developers with essential capital while ensuring buyers have access to a reliable supply of carbon removal credits. Peter Reinhardt, CEO of Charm Industrial, highlighted the validation this partnership offers for building the necessary infrastructure for a permanent carbon removal industry.

As corporate demand for carbon removal rises, particularly among technology companies, the gap between supply and demand remains a critical issue. With analysts estimating that demand could skyrocket to 100 million metric tons per year by 2030, the current market is only a fraction of that potential. The financing aspect of the JPMorgan-Charm deal is vital, as carbon removal projects require substantial upfront investments. Innovative financing models are emerging, resembling the early days of renewable energy, which could catalyze the next wave of growth in this sector. Overall, the JPMorgan-Charm Industrial agreement illustrates the transition of carbon removal from a niche solution to a more established and investable market.

June 10 2026: JPMorgan's Lake Predicts Slow Adoption of Agentic Commerce

Marianne Lake, CEO of JPMorgan Chase's consumer and community banking division, expressed skepticism regarding the swift adoption of agentic commerce during her recent address at a Morgan Stanley investor conference. On 10th June 2026, she highlighted the rapid acceptance of artificial intelligence platforms in streamlining the search and discovery process for online purchases, attributing this momentum to their ability to reduce friction for users.

However, Lake cautioned that this trend has not yet translated into the transactional phase of online shopping, where AI agents would autonomously make purchases on behalf of consumers. She emphasized that trust and security will play critical roles in this evolution, stating, "When people are moving money, things change. Trust and security matter even more." This sentiment indicates that consumers may be hesitant to delegate purchasing decisions to AI agents in the near future.

Lake emphasized the importance of preserving customer protections and payment preferences as JPMorgan Chase explores agentic-enabled commerce. The bank is focused on ensuring human oversight remains in critical transactions and that transparency exists regarding agent actions. She stated, "We have to establish a liability framework that works if an agent makes a mistake," underscoring the complexities involved in integrating AI within the consumer payment ecosystem.

In the context of travel arrangements, Lake noted that while discovery remains challenging, JPMorgan's data capabilities and partnerships could play a vital role in simplifying the process for customers. The bank plans to pilot a consumer-facing AI travel agent before the end of the year, with Lake affirming that identifying problems to solve will be key to achieving rapid scaling in this area.

As JPMorgan navigates the evolving landscape of AI-driven commerce, Lake recognized the dual nature of competition. While AI reduces barriers to entry, allowing fintechs and new entrants to innovate quickly, it also empowers JPMorgan to modernize its operations and respond swiftly to market demands. She mentioned that the bank continues to strive for a 15% share of U.S.consumer deposits by expanding into new markets and enhancing its offerings, while remaining vigilant against competitive threats.

June 09 2026: JPMorgan's Executive Highlights Consumer Vigilance Amid Inflation Concerns

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is maintaining a vigilant stance regarding consumer health, as concerns over inflation continue to loom. On 9th June 2026, Marianne Lake, CEO of the bank's consumer and community banking division, addressed these issues during her remarks at the Morgan Stanley U.S. Financials Conference in New York City.

Lake noted that while U.S.consumers have shown resilience and spending remains solid, there is a diminishing segment of the population for whom wage growth is failing to keep pace with rising inflation. "You're not seeing anything right now, but you are being very, very watchful. If inflation were to be higher for longer, this sort of trend of wages keeping up with inflation could be at some risk," Lake stated, emphasizing the need for caution.

The context of these remarks comes as U.S. inflation has surged at its fastest rate in three years, largely driven by escalating energy prices related to geopolitical tensions. This inflationary environment is eroding household incomes and has the potential to stifle consumer spending and overall economic growth. Lake's commentary aligns with insights shared by Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon, who indicated a possible shift in consumer behavior in the latter half of 2026 if inflation remains elevated.

Lake further highlighted that the financial buffers that consumers had established during the pandemic have now normalized, resulting in a reduced capacity to absorb future economic shocks. She pointed out that while the unemployment rate remains low, there is a noticeable softening in labor demand. "While the unemployment is low, demand for labor is a little softer," she remarked, underscoring the evolving labor landscape.

Despite these challenges, Lake expressed optimism regarding JPMorgan's product demand, forecasting that loan growth in 2026 is expected to outpace industry averages. She also mentioned that higher tax refunds and lower tax bills have somewhat mitigated the impact of rising energy costs, particularly for lower-income customers, who have spent approximately 20% to 25% of their incremental funds resulting from tax refunds in the early months of increased energy prices. "So time is a big vector here," she concluded.

headline: It was a good day for Argentina's country risk and stocks, but the tech sector took a hit
story_html:
This Thursday, the Argentine market was buoyed by optimism, coupled with a favorable international environment, and broke through the 430-point mark.

The country risk premium fell by six units to 429 basis points (-1.8%) , according to Rava Bursátil's screens. The last time the indicator compiled by JP Morgan showed similar values was on April 30, 2018, during Mauricio Macri's presidency, when it closed at 430 units. As a result, it approached its low under Javier Milei's administration, when it hit 425 points last Monday.

This movement was a result of sovereign bond yields. Bonds issued under local law rose as much as 0.9%, led by the AL41D. Meanwhile, Global bonds fell as much as 0.5% (GD46D), while the GD46D climbed 1%.

Meanwhile, Argentine stocks listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ADRs) traded in positive territory, in line with the major Wall Street indices. BBVA led the pack with a 4.1% gain, followed by Banco Macro ( +3.2%), Loma Negra ( +2%), and Edenor ( +1.7%). Telecom (-5.6%), Tenaris (-3.2%), and Ternium (-2.5%) fell.

The most striking development was Globant's 11.2% drop. This was not due to any specific announcement by the company, but rather because Accenture released its latest earnings report, which was received negatively by the markets, causing its shares to plummet 18%. As one of the industry's leading players, it dragged down technology services companies, as was the case with IBM (-5%).

The Merval rose 1.3% to close at 3,337,448.40, equivalent to US$2,216.96 when adjusted for the spot dollar with settlement (+1.2%). The biggest gains were in the financial sector: BBVA (+4.5%), Banco Macro (+4.4%), and Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos (+3.4%). Transener (-0.9%) and YPF (-0.9%) fell (-3.9%).

Analyst Fernando Marull noted that the performance of Argentine stocks and bonds reflects the recent positive financial news . The most recent development was a US$2 billion guarantee package to enable Argentina to refinance its debt payments. This "triggered the rebound," along with the Central Bank's (BCRA) steady purchase of foreign exchange reserves and the upgrade of Argentina's debt rating. Meanwhile, the global mood was "slightly better" today following the agreement between the U.S. and Iran to end the conflict in the Middle East.

Fernando Camusso noted that "the market isn't rising because of today's data; it's rising because it's positioning itself ahead of June 23," which is when… "If MSCI upgrades Argentina to Frontier Market status, it will open the door to foreign capital inflows that are currently barred from investing in Argentine assets due to regulatory restrictions , " he noted.

Dollar Today

Various exchange rates trended upward during Thursday's trading session. The official retail dollar rate rose by $10 (+0.7%) and closed at $1,470 for sale at Banco Nación. The average bank rate hovered around $1,470.01, according to the Central Bank's (BCRA) daily survey of financial institutions.

Meanwhile, the wholesale rate stood at $1,450.62, up $9.32 from its opening value (0.7%). As a result, it was 19% below the upper limit of the exchange rate band, set today at $1,788.47.

The MEP dollar rose by $5.43 (+0.4%) and appeared on screens at $1,467.06. The contado with settlement (CCL) remained stable and traded at $1,506.68.

Meanwhile, the blue dollar rose by $10 (+0.7%) and was trading in Buenos Aires' financial district at $1,485 for sale. Since last Friday, it has accumulated a gain of $35 and reached its highest level since late February.

headline: June 20, 2026: KOREA INVESTMENT CORPORATION & PEERS: LATEST INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENTS
story_html:
NEWS BITES - PRIVATE COMPANIES

Korea Investment Corporation and J.P. Morgan Asset Management held a Global Market Outlook seminar on June 9, 2026, at the InterContinental Parnas in Seoul to connect with retail investors and present market forecasts. The event featured insights from J.P. Morgan strategists, who highlighted that as the artificial intelligence industry transitions from the training phase to the inference phase, investment opportunities will emerge across networking, computing, memory, and power infrastructure. A key feature of the seminar was the introduction of the Korea Investment JPMorgan U.S. Tech Fund, which leverages J.P. Morgan's global research to invest in companies within the AI ecosystem. Approximately 300 billion won has been invested in this product recently, pushing the total assets under management beyond 560 billion won alongside the Korea Investment JPMorgan Global High Yield Fund. Korea Investment Corporation President Kim Sung-hwan emphasized their commitment to not merely selling financial products but rather becoming a strategic partner that introduces premier investment opportunities aimed at fostering long-term growth of clients' investment assets.

In another strategic move within the technology sector, Korea Investment Trust Management announced plans to participate in SpaceX's initial public offering ahead of the planned listing on June 12, 2026. The firm will allocate shares acquired through the IPO to its ACE U.S. Space Tech Active ETF and the Korea Investment Global Space Technology & Defense Fund. The anticipated IPO is expected to raise between $75 billion to $80 billion, with a projected valuation nearing $1.75 trillion to $2 trillion. Korea Investment Trust Management aims to increase SpaceX's representation in its ETF to as much as 25 percent. The offering price will be determined on June 11, and the firm is considering additional purchases as the market opens. Kim Hyun-tae, head of global quant management at Korea Investment Trust Management, stated, "Because both funds are active, they can respond immediately on the day SpaceX lists."

Further expanding its global footprint, Korea Investment & Securities Co. joined forces with Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and Barclays in a significant financing initiative for Carlyle Group's BASF investment on June 3, 2026. This partnership occurs as the brokerage unit of Korea Investment Holdings reported record earnings for 2025, becoming the first domestic securities firm to surpass 2 trillion won in profits. The firm is also witnessing a sharp recovery in South Korea's venture capital sector, with leading firms reporting a V-shaped rebound driven by favorable equity market conditions.

Among industry peers, China Investment Corporation (CIC) has also seen significant transactional activity. On April 15, 2026, Goldman Sachs and Ardian successfully acquired a $1 billion portfolio from CIC at notable discounts. Ardian secured the assets at a double-digit discount, while Goldman achieved a single-digit discount. CIC has been rebalancing its portfolio to reduce its exposure to illiquid US dollar-denominated holdings. For Goldman Sachs Asset Management, this adds to a track record of over 750 secondary transactions and more than $80 billion in deployed capital, while Ardian recently raised a record $30 billion secondary fund.

In parallel, BlueFive Capital was appointed as the first General Partner for a Fund of Funds established by CICC Capital, the private equity arm of China International Capital Corporation, in partnership with Chinese steelmaker HBIS Group. During a ceremony in Beijing on January 6, 2026, it was announced that the fund aims to raise RMB 32 billion (approximately $4.58 billion) over a 15-year term. Structured around industry-finance synergy, central-local cooperation, and cross-border linkage, the fund will deploy capital in advanced materials, new energy, and next-generation information technology. Hazem Ben-Gacem, Founder and Chief Executive of BlueFive Capital, stated, "We are bullish about China's long-term growth potential and see significant opportunities for HBIS Group's cross-border expansion, particularly in high-end manufacturing and new building materials."

Additionally, foreign direct investment from China and Hong Kong in Canada recently exceeded $60 billion, making these regions the third-largest source of overseas capital in the country. Statistics Canada reported the investment stock from China at $24.9 billion, while Hong Kong contributed $32.8 billion. On December 30, 2025, Invest Alberta noted that these investments are primarily focused on Alberta's traditional oil and gas sector, carbon capture projects, green energy initiatives, and tourism development. Prime Minister Mark Carney met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in October 2025, and Global Affairs officials are reportedly preparing for a potential Carney visit to China in 2026 to further diplomatic engagement.

story_html:

Prometheus' round also includes Goldman Sachs and BlackRock among its backers, highlighting a broader wave of interest in industrial AI from leading institutions.

The deal aligns with JPMorgan's broader strategy to weave technology into core operations, including tokenization and digital platforms, and could bolster its investment-banking and lending franchises if AI tools in industry gain wider traction.

Market reaction was visible in the stock, with JPMorgan closing at US$320.72, up 2.7% over the last week, 6.8% over the past month and 23.4% year-to-date, underscoring investor enthusiasm.
